content.text:
Yes—**I found two community MCP servers specifically for Graphite’s art editor.**

| Option | What it enables | Main limitation |
|---|---|---|
| [graphite-editor-mcp](https://github.com/ktheunlikedoll/graphite-editor-mcp) | Generate procedural backgrounds from parameters or node graphs, discover available nodes, and render batches of variations to PNG/SVG/JPG/GIF. | Requires building a pinned Graphite engine locally. |
| [graphite-art-mcp](https://github.com/ACoci86/graphite-art-mcp) | Work in a visible editor: create editable layers, change colors and positioning, preview, undo, and export. | Its exposed tools currently lack gradients, blend modes, and general procedural node editing. |

**For the backgrounds you’re imagining, I’d investigate `graphite-editor-mcp` first.** It already includes noise patterns and duotone backgrounds, plus custom node graphs—so we could ask for several variations with different palettes, seeds, and scales, then choose a result. Its documentation does flag an engine crash after export that the wrapper handles by validating the generated file; I’d test actual renders before relying on it. [Project documentation](https://github.com/ktheunlikedoll/graphite-editor-mcp)

We could also use browser automation to operate **editor.graphite.art directly**, though that would need testing against its canvas and node interface.

Both MCP projects are unofficial and use local Graphite builds; they don’t simply connect to an existing tab on the public site. I’ve checked their documentation, but haven’t installed or tested either. [Editor connector architecture](https://github.com/ACoci86/graphite-art-mcp/blob/main/docs/development.md), [headless integration](https://github.com/ktheunlikedoll/graphite-editor-mcp#integration)
okay connect and try making  a few different background options for baste
I’ll connect the procedural Graphite renderer, inspect Baste’s visual direction, and generate a few distinct background options for you to compare.

+# Baste × Graphite material studies
+
+Four background families derived from Baste's existing atelier direction in
+`PRODUCT.md` and `site/src/global.css`: warm pattern paper, ink, red basting
+thread and blue tailor's chalk. The reserved reading area is the left 56%.
+
+The originals are generated by Graphite, through real `graphite-editor-mcp`
+stdio calls. The comparison sheets use Pillow for resizing and labels only.
+The source documents, exact seeds, render hashes and exit metadata are kept
+alongside the candidates so the assets can be regenerated.
+
+## Materials
+
+- **Flax linen:** quiet paper grain and repeated warp/weft, with a red edge seam.
+- **Cutting room:** warm pattern stock, garment contours and seam allowances.
+- **Chalk draft:** cool paper, blue pattern contours and measurement marks.
+- **Ink selvedge:** warm charcoal cloth, woven structure and loose red stitching.
+
+Five rounds per family progressively tune the grain and pattern opacity while
+varying seeds and contour placement. Final selection is a subjective visual
+review against the repository's weighted criteria, not a hosted judge score.
+
+## Connection and reproduction
+
+The connector is installed at `~/.local/share/graphite-editor-mcp`, with upstream
+engine commit `d7ae6029e0c1818d81a13b0389ef1808496a715b` and the connector's
+versioned node-metadata patch. It is registered with Codex as `graphite-editor`.
+The study script itself opens the same server using the MCP SDK over stdio.
+
+From the Baste project root:
+
+```sh
+rtk proxy node assets/output/graphite-baste-20261001/source/render.mjs inspect
+rtk proxy node assets/output/graphite-baste-20261001/source/render.mjs draft
+rtk proxy node assets/output/graphite-baste-20261001/source/render.mjs final
+```
+
+The first engine build on this machine needed `/usr/bin` ahead of the Guix
+compiler utilities, and explicit GCC selection:
+
+```sh
+rtk proxy env PATH=/usr/bin:/home/diogenes/.nix-profile/bin:/bin CC=/usr/bin/gcc CXX=/usr/bin/g++ 'REDACTED -Clinker=/usr/bin/gcc' CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 bash scripts/fetch-engine.sh
+```
+
+Run that last command inside the connector installation when rebuilding.
+It is not needed for normal rendering after installation.
+
+## Delivery boundaries
+
+These are static, full-frame compositions. They are not certified as seamless
+tiles. Place them using `background-size: cover`; crop-test against the actual
+page before adoption. The dark material requires light text. PNG originals and
+the legacy `.graphite` sources are preserved; current public-editor import
+compatibility is unverified. No website styles are changed by this study.
+
+Sources: [Graphite](https://graphite.art/),
+[connector and engine build](https://github.com/ktheunlikedoll/graphite-editor-mcp),
+[Codex MCP configuration](https://developers.openai.com/codex/mcp/).
